mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances with positive RSAFS growth, or RSAFS growth does not correlate with earnings growth (Pearson's r < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE < 5% does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a contraction in economic activity, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO MoM decline does not correlate with subsequent earnings reports.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening economy with increased consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with subsequent consumer spending data.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS increase does not correlate with subsequent corporate earnings reports.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a single month signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with subsequent consumer spending data.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter signals robust economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or GDPC1 growth does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.
